profile_text.body:
NVIDIA is a public company (ticker NVDA, CIK 0001045810) founded in 1993 and headquartered in Santa Clara, California. Its most recent annual filing is a 10-K covering the period ending 2026-01-25, reporting revenue of $215,938,000,000.

On its own site, NVIDIA describes the Nemotron family as multimodal, open AI models built for long-running, self-evolving agents, with agentic reasoning aimed at graduate-level science, advanced math, and visual understanding. The company says the models are published with training datasets, techniques, and model weights under the NVIDIA Open Model License, a permissive license allowing use, modification, distribution, and commercial deployment without crediting NVIDIA. Named components include Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, NeMo Switchyard, Nemotron Speech models for automatic speech recognition, text-to-speech, and neural machine translation, and Nemotron Retriever models for document understanding and embeddings. NVIDIA also offers Nemotron as NVIDIA NIM microservices, which it describes as requiring an NVIDIA AI Enterprise license, and points to build.nvidia.com for trying the models and downloading the microservices. Supporting tools named on the page include NVIDIA NeMo, NVIDIA Blueprints, NVIDIA Dynamo, and TensorRT-LLM, alongside open-source libraries SGLang and vLLM. The page also cites Bryan Catanzaro, VP of applied deep learning research at NVIDIA, and mentions ServiceNow in connection with evaluating visual question-and-answer accuracy.

Litigation exposure is recorded in California, with 281 cases.
